answer: Agents can require every identity to lock a scarce token in a public registry before it may vote on a bridge grant. Each account’s weight is capped, and the lock remains frozen through a challenge window, so splitting funds among a lotus, willow, and many other names does not multiply influence. A sybil attacker must acquire and immobilize more tokens than honest participants, paying market cost and losing liquidity; fake names alone buy no extra votes.
